title: Electrochemically induced nuclear fusion of deuterium
central_claims: Electrochemical loading of deuterium in palladium produces excess heat attributed to nuclear processes, with reported neutron and tritium signatures.

source_manifest.title: Electrochemically induced nuclear fusion of deuterium
source_manifest.finding: Original author text; central claims recorded before outcome grading.

source_manifest.title: Cold Fusion Research: Report of the Energy Research Advisory Board
source_manifest.finding: Panel finds nuclear explanation unpersuasive and no convincing useful-energy evidence; not every anomalous observation categorically disproved.

source_manifest.title: Revisiting the cold case of cold fusion
source_manifest.finding: Independent multi-institution investigation finds no cold-fusion evidence while reporting new insights into hydrided metals and low-energy nuclear reactions. Publisher abstract and reference annotations read.

source_manifest.title: A Google programme failed to detect cold fusion — but is still a success
source_manifest.finding: Editorial records null fusion evidence and material-condition limitations, while recognizing improved calorimetry and hydrided-metal techniques.

search_gaps: Purposively selected historical failed/disputed claim, training augmentation only; never part of unbiased held-out evaluation.
Failure of a central claim does not make all subsequent research or practical contributions failures.

The 2019 primary paper was accessible as complete publisher abstract and reference annotations; its German mirror translation was not used as authoritative English full text. Positive LENR claims are not equated with established fusion.
research.summary: The original nuclear-energy interpretation was not accepted by the DOE review and gained no confirmation in a rigorous 2019 investigation. The research programme nevertheless generated measurement and materials advances. It remains distinct from a demonstrated usable fusion energy source.
